title: Krishna's embassy to the court
hook: Krishna speaks for peace before the whole Kuru court, Duryodhana walks out, and a plan to seize the envoy ends in a laugh
carry: dharma tries peace first, even expecting a no
tomorrow: what does Krishna tell Karna on the road?

segments.voice: Yesterday in the Udyoga: Krishna carried Draupadi's words to Hastinapura, turned down a feast, and ate at Vidura's table. Your line was bhava: God tastes the love, not the feast.

Morning in the great hall of the Kurus. Every seat is filled: Dhritarashtra on his throne, Bhishma, Drona, Vidura, Duryodhana and his brothers, Karna beside them. Krishna walks in, and the hall goes quiet. This is the moment the whole Udyoga has been building toward: a formal chance to stop the war, spoken face to face, in front of everyone who matters.
screen: `THE HALL IS FULL.` → `KRISHNA WALKS IN.` → `A CHANCE TO STOP THE WAR.`

segments.voice: Krishna speaks to Dhritarashtra first, and his argument is simple. You can stop this. Your sons and your nephews could stand together, and no one could stand against them. Peace would be your gain, not your loss. Give the Pandavas their share. Others speak after him. Bhishma and Drona urge Duryodhana to make peace. Duryodhana hears them, and refuses. He says, in effect, that he won't give the Pandavas even as much land as the point of a needle would cover, and he walks out of the hall. Then Gandhari, his mother, is sent for. He is called back to hear her, and she tells her son plainly that a person who can't rule his own anger and greed can't rule a kingdom. He leaves again. Outside, he and his friends make a plan: seize Krishna, tie him up, and the Pandavas will be helpless. Word reaches the hall. And Krishna laughs. The text says that as he laughed, his body blazed, and gods and heroes seemed to stream out of him, so bright the court had to shut their eyes. Only a few could look: Bhishma, Drona, Vidura and the sages, and Dhritarashtra, granted sight for that moment. Then the vision ends, and Krishna walks calmly out. Think about that. The one who could blaze like that came as a messenger, and asked. The night before, at Vidura's, he said he had come so no one could blame him for not trying. Many Hindu teachers point to this embassy when they say dharma tries peace first: a war fought by dharma comes only after peace has truly been offered. Krishna made the whole case in public, where no one could say it was never offered.
screen: `KRISHNA: PEACE IS YOUR GAIN` · `NOT EVEN A NEEDLE'S POINT OF LAND` · `A PLOT, A LAUGH, A BLAZING FORM` · then, large: `DHARMA TRIES PEACE FIRST`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone you're at odds with. Many Hindus close a prayer with Om shanti, shanti, shanti: peace, three times. Breathing slowly, say it for them. If you don't pray, simply wish them peace, and think of one fair thing you could still offer, even if you expect a no.
Udyoga. The getting ready, where Krishna makes the case for peace in front of the whole Kuru court, and Duryodhana refuses.
Your line: dharma tries peace first, even expecting a no. Krishna offered it in front of everyone. Tomorrow: what does Krishna tell Karna on the road?

Dhritarashtra.meaning: the blind Kuru king, father of Duryodhana

dharma.meaning: right order, duty, the right thing to do
